title: COPY callback returns UNAVAILABLE when devCtx active: use-after-free on hash copy
description:
Trigger: WOLF_CRYPTO_CB_COPY enabled + hardware hash active (not TLS-safe mode) + wc_Sha256Copy() called (e.g., TLS 1.3 transcript hash).

WC_ALGO_TYPE_COPY handler returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE unconditionally (crypto2dev_port.c:1523). wolfSSL then falls back to a bitwise memcpy of the wc_Sha256 struct, which copies the devCtx pointer verbatim. Now both the original and the copy point to the same Crypto2DevHashCtx that holds a live op_fd.

When either object is Finalized or Freed: close(ctx->op_fd) closes the fd, ctx is XFREEd, *devctx_ptr = NULL on THAT object only. The other object still holds the stale pointer. Next operation on the other object: dereferences freed ctx (use-after-free) and then double-closes the fd (which may now be an unrelated open fd reused by the OS).

TLS-safe mode (g_tls_safe_mode=1) prevents hardware hash for WOLF_CRYPTO2DEV_DEVID objects, which prevents the scenario for TLS uses. But non-TLS users who enable hardware hash and call wc_Sha256Copy hit this.

Fix: In the WC_ALGO_TYPE_COPY case, check if the source object has a non-NULL devCtx. If so, return WC_HW_E (hard failure) rather than CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE, so wolfSSL surfaces an error instead of silently creating a corrupt copy.
